bands.label: Early
bands.sentence: The work that matters still lives in people's heads. The first useful move is to write one workflow down and name who owns it.

bands.label: Forming
bands.sentence: Pieces of the work are written down. A named owner and one system of record are what turn that into something a team can run.

bands.label: Ready
bands.sentence: The business can put a new system to work. The open question is which workflow to start with, and who owns it day to day.

bands.label: Running
bands.sentence: A real workflow already uses the tools. The next gain is the job that still waits on one person.

suggestions.title: Start with where the knowledge lives
suggestions.body: Where the knowledge lives is the part that would stall a new system. Write down one real example this week: the source, the owner, and the step that happens next.

suggestions.title: Tighten where the knowledge lives
suggestions.body: Where the knowledge lives is partly in place. Name the gap in one sentence and pick the person who closes it before you add a tool.

suggestions.title: Start with whether the work is written down
suggestions.body: Whether the work is written down is the part that would stall a new system. Write down one real example this week: the source, the owner, and the step that happens next.

suggestions.title: Tighten whether the work is written down
suggestions.body: Whether the work is written down is partly in place. Name the gap in one sentence and pick the person who closes it before you add a tool.

suggestions.title: Start with who would own a new system
suggestions.body: Who would own a new system is the part that would stall a new system. Write down one real example this week: the source, the owner, and the step that happens next.

suggestions.title: Tighten who would own a new system
suggestions.body: Who would own a new system is partly in place. Name the gap in one sentence and pick the person who closes it before you add a tool.

suggestions.title: Start with who decides and how fast
suggestions.body: Who decides and how fast is the part that would stall a new system. Write down one real example this week: the source, the owner, and the step that happens next.

suggestions.title: Tighten who decides and how fast
suggestions.body: Who decides and how fast is partly in place. Name the gap in one sentence and pick the person who closes it before you add a tool.

suggestions.title: You can put a system to work
suggestions.body: Data, process, people, and the decision are far enough along. The useful next step is one workflow, with a named owner, running this quarter.

suggestions.title: New customers come from one place
suggestions.body: When referrals are the whole pipeline, a quiet month is a quiet quarter. Write down the one other place buyers already look, and put a page there that answers their question.

suggestions.title: AI answer engines are unchecked
suggestions.body: Ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google the question a buyer would ask, using your product words. Save what comes back. That is the baseline the site scan is measuring.

suggestions.title: The site cannot keep up with the work
suggestions.body: If a change takes weeks, the pages that should answer buyers stay stale. List the three pages a buyer hits first and who can publish a change to them.

suggestions.title: Still reading your site
suggestions.body: The scan is still running. Open the full scan when it finishes. The rest of this check does not wait on it.

suggestions.title: The site scan did not finish
suggestions.body: We could not score the site this time. Run the scan directly and the visibility section will fill in.

suggestions.title: No json ld home
suggestions.body: The home page has no structured data, so answer engines have to guess what the business is. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: No org schema
suggestions.body: There is no Organization or LocalBusiness markup naming who you are, where you are, and how to reach you. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Missing faq schema
suggestions.body: The questions buyers ask are not marked up as answers a machine can quote. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Missing llms txt
suggestions.body: There is no llms.txt file telling an answer engine which pages matter. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Empty llms txt
suggestions.body: llms.txt exists but says nothing useful. Name the pages a buyer should read. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Missing llms full
suggestions.body: A short llms.txt is present. A fuller llms-full.txt gives answer engines the longer context. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Sitemap missing
suggestions.body: No sitemap was found, so crawlers have to discover pages by links alone. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Sitemap unparseable
suggestions.body: A sitemap was found but could not be read. Publish a valid XML sitemap. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Robots blocks gptbot
suggestions.body: robots.txt blocks GPTBot, so that answer engine is told to stay out. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Robots blocks ai bots
suggestions.body: robots.txt blocks one or more AI crawlers. Decide which ones you want reading the site. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Low json ld coverage
suggestions.body: Most pages have no structured data, so the site looks thin to a machine. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Pages fetch failed
suggestions.body: Some important pages could not be fetched. If a buyer cannot load them, neither can a crawler. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Missing breadcrumb
suggestions.body: Pages do not say where they sit in the site, which makes the structure harder to quote. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Missing howto schema
suggestions.body: Step-by-step pages are not marked as HowTo, so the steps are harder to cite. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Missing product schema
suggestions.body: Product pages do not carry Product markup for price, availability, and name. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

offers.said: Your process is real, and off-the-shelf software does not fit it.
offers.build: A system shaped by the way you already work, including the exceptions.

offers.said: Answers wait on two or three people.
offers.build: A correct answer from knowledge you own, on text or voice, without growing the team in proportion to the questions.

offers.said: New people do not sound like your best people.
offers.build: The talk track, the booking, and a coach on the live book of business, so a new person sells to the standard.

offers.said: Leads arrive with no story attached.
offers.build: An assessment a person finishes, a result they can read, and a path to a conversation.

offers.said: You do not know if AI answer engines can find you.
offers.build: A scan of how readable the site is to answer engines, and the fixes that move the score. pirx.ca went from near-zero to 201K search impressions, 1.1K clicks, and 21.8K impressions on Google's Generative AI surface in about twelve weeks.

offers.said: Decisions wait on last month's numbers.
offers.build: The number you need while the decision is still open, from the record you already keep.

offers.said: A new channel feels like it needs a department.
offers.build: Creative, language, and the claims you allow, produced from a system that already knows them.

offers.said: The sale still needs a visit before anyone says yes.
offers.build: Fit, price, booking, and trust on the screen, before anyone gets in a car.

offers.said: The vendor bill grows as you grow.
offers.build: Answers, agreements, and the customer record on your side of the wall.

offers.said: One person knows how the important thing works.
offers.build: The knowledge becomes something a customer can finish and a team can teach.

offers.said: Fraud or order review eats someone's morning.
offers.build: Low-risk orders clear themselves. High-risk orders reach a person with the history already assembled.

offers.said: Claims drift the moment someone new writes.
offers.build: Writing fenced by the claims, the voice, and the product rules you already approved.

copy.landingTitle: Is your business ready to put AI to work?
copy.landingDeck: A five-to-seven-minute check. You get a score for readiness, growth, and how readable your website is to AI answer engines, plus three things to do in each.
copy.consent: We'll send this report and, if you book, the notes from your session. Nothing else.
copy.bookingTitle: Book a working session — thirty minutes, bring the workflow, we leave with a brief.
